title: Homogeneous internal functions with injective underlying coefficients are equivariantly injective
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a profinite group, write $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$, and use internal $A$-modules and their internal $G$-actions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $J$ be such an equivariant module whose underlying internal $A$-module $UJ$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a condensed set $X$, write $A[X]$ for the free internal $A$-module, left adjoint to forgetting a module to a condensed set. Internal module Hom means the right adjoint of internal tensor [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. For each integer $n\geq0$ equip
$$H_n(J)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{n+1}],UJ)$$
with the action, interpreted after every profinite base change,
$$(g\cdot f)(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=g\cdot_J f(g^{-1}g_0,\ldots,g^{-1}g_n).$$
Then $H_n(J)$ is an injective object in the category of internal $G$-equivariant $A$-modules. No projectivity of the free internal module, discreteness of $J$, or finiteness of $G$ is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-internal-homogeneous-lift-reconstruction], the prescribed homogeneous action has a normalized model $H$ with underlying module $H_n(J)$. Fix any equivariant monomorphism $i:N\hookrightarrow M$ and equivariant linear map $h:N\to H$. We solve its extension problem using the same free modules and slice evaluations as in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image, homogeneous-function injectivity: existence of the specified homogeneous action

proof.text: Put $P_n=A[\underline G^n]$. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-homogeneous-transpose-extension] to $A,G,n,J,H,i,h$. Its sole injectivity hypothesis is the assumed injectivity of $UJ$. It supplies $\alpha:P_n\otimes_A UN\to UJ$ and $\beta:P_n\otimes_A UM\to UJ$ with $\beta\circ(P_n\otimes_A Ui)=\alpha$ and $\alpha([\mathbf t]\otimes x)=h(x)(1,\mathbf t)$ on every profinite slice. Thus $\beta([\mathbf t]\otimes i(x))=h(x)(1,\mathbf t)$ after every base change.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image, homogeneous-function injectivity: transpose extension, old steps 1-5

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-internal-homogeneous-lift-reconstruction] with this $\beta$. It gives the equivariant internal map $b_\beta:M\to H$ specified on every slice by
$$b_\beta(m)(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=g_0\cdot_J\beta([g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_0^{-1}g_n]\otimes(g_0^{-1}\cdot_M m)).$$
Its restriction clause applies to exactly the equality from the preceding step, yielding $b_\beta\circ i=h$. For each monomorphism $i$, this constructs a preimage of every $h$ under restriction $\operatorname{Hom}(M,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(N,H)$. This restriction is therefore surjective for every $i$, exactly the injectivity condition of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus $H$, with the specified homogeneous-function module and action, is injective.
